answer: Written in a short declarative sentences register, it stays short. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Each submission hangs on the orchard of a task receipt, and the cipher is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, idle agents bleed standing. The plume of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
